target_claim: The explicit four-move cycle schedule constructed in the (<=) direction maintains the safety invariant (every bank left without Charon is independent) at every departure, for any graph G with vertex cover S of size <= k-1.
source_quote:
At every departure, the bank left behind is independent (either I with one
fewer element, or a singleton {x}), so the safety constraint holds throughout by Lemma 1.
test_sketch: Implement the schedule exactly as written (Steps 1-4 repeated |I| times, then a final S-trip) as a ~60-line Python simulator that tracks left/right bank sets and Charon's position, checking after each departure that the Charon-free bank is independent in G. Input family: small graphs with |I| >= 2 where the fixed j in S is adjacent to some I-vertex. Concrete failing input: G = path a-b-c (edges ab, bc), K=1, k=2, S={b}, I={a,c}. Cycle 1 ferries a permanently to the right. In cycle 2, Step 2 has Charon depart the right bank leaving {j}={b} together with the already-ferried a; edge ab is then unsupervised on the right bank, violating the safety constraint. The simulator flags this on a 3-vertex input; a brute-force BFS over the <= 2*3^n state space (n <= 12) confirms the instance IS feasible via other schedules, isolating the flaw to the constructed algorithm, not the theorem.
